newsitem.title: INDIA: India scraps equity floor for state agencies.
newsitem.headline: India scraps equity floor for state agencies.

text.p: India's Industry Ministry said on Wednesday state agencies would no longer need to hold at least 26 percent of the equity of joint ventures they promote.
Current policy requires state agencies including the State Industrial Development Corp to hold at least 26 percent of the paid up equity capital of companies which they promote.
The ministry said in a statement that the government had done away with the stipulation "in line with the liberalised policy". It did not elaborate.
"While applying for the industrial licence, the state government agency may indicate the extent of equity holding proposed to be held by it in the joint venture," the ministry said.
